**Kapselendoskopi** (capsule endoscopy) is a diagnostic medical procedure utilized in the Danish healthcare system for the comprehensive evaluation of children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Within the national quality assurance framework, it serves as a recognized alternative to [[mr-af-tyndtarmen|MR af tyndtarmen]] (magnetic resonance imaging of the small intestine) for visualizing the small bowel [^src1]. 

The procedure is a core component of [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]], a quality metric that assesses whether pediatric IBD patients receive a complete diagnostic workup [^src2]. To fulfill the criteria for this indicator, a diagnosis must be established through a colonoscopy, supplemented by a gastroscopy, and either an MR scan of the small intestine or capsule endoscopy [^src1]. In the Danish national health registries, capsule endoscopy and MR enterography are tracked using a specific set of SKS procedure codes, including KUJD02/05, KUJF32/35, UXMD25*, WMAMPXYXX, and KUJF92 [^src2]. 

Despite its established role in clinical guidelines, the implementation of small bowel imaging remains a systemic challenge in Danish IBD care. According to the DANIBD 2025 report, the failure to perform an MR scan or capsule endoscopy is the primary reason for incomplete diagnostic workups, accounting for 48% of the missing cases that prevent departments from meeting the quality indicator targets [^src2]. This shortfall highlights ongoing regional and local variations in adhering to evidence-based diagnostic recommendations for pediatric IBD patients.
